title: Distordia Article Standard (v0.2.0 draft)
description: Successor draft to article.v0.1.0. PRIMARY model: an article is a content anchor (content.v0.2.0, kind=article) whose body is stored off-chain on a decentralized store (Arweave/IPFS) and integrity-checked by the on-chain 'hash'. This removes the v0.1.0 chunk-chain's fragility (orphan chunks, partial-delete holes, no integrity, 5000-char cap). The hardened on-chain chunk chain below is retained ONLY as an optional fully-on-chain fallback for censorship-resistance maximalists. See docs/content-cluster-design-note.md.

primaryModel.description: Recommended: publish the body to Arweave/IPFS and register ONE content.v0.2.0 asset with kind=article, cid, hash, author(namespace), title. Unbounded length, integrity, low cost, and verifiable like any other content.

maxSize: 1KB per asset (system fields ~180 bytes, ~820 bytes for data).
fallbackModel: Fully-on-chain linked chain, HARDENED vs v0.1.0: every asset carries 'article-id' and the chunks carry a 'root' back-pointer and 'seq' order, and the root carries 'article-hash' over the assembled body, so the chain is attributable and integrity-checkable. Publish is still non-atomic across assets -- clients MUST verify the full chain (contiguous seq, matching article-id, article-hash) before display.

assetTypes.description: Root article asset (on-chain fallback). Holds metadata, the first text chunk, and an integrity hash over the full assembled body.

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's register address.

article-id.description: Stable article identifier. Every chunk references it, so any chunk is attributable to its article (fixes the v0.1.0 orphan/unattributable problem).

author.description: Author NAMESPACE. Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

text.description: First text chunk of the body (max 320 chars given added metadata).

article-hash.description: SHA-256 over the full assembled body (all chunks concatenated). Lets a reader detect a broken/tampered/partial chain (the v0.1.0 integrity gap).

reply-to.description: self-addr of post/article being replied to.

next.description: self-addr of the first continuation chunk (empty if the article fits the root).

supersedes.description: self-addr of the prior article revision.

assetTypes.description: Continuation chunk (on-chain fallback). Now attributable (article-id + root back-pointer) and ordered (seq).

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's register address.

article-id.description: Article this chunk belongs to (back-reference; an isolated chunk is now attributable).

root.description: self-addr of the root distordia-article asset.

seq.description: Chunk order index (1-based). Lets a reader verify a contiguous, complete chain.

next.description: self-addr of the next chunk (empty for the last).

nexus.reassembly: Prefer the content-anchor model (fetch body by cid, verify hash). For the fallback chain: collect all chunks WHERE article-id = root.article-id, order by seq, verify contiguity and that the concatenation matches article-hash, then render.

notes: Primary model removes the 5000-char cap, orphan chunks, partial-delete holes, and the integrity gap by storing the body off-chain (decentralized) with an on-chain hash.
Fallback chain adds article-id, root back-pointer, seq, and article-hash so even the fully-on-chain path is attributable and integrity-checkable.
Successor draft to article.v0.1.0 (standards/article-standard.json), retained for history.
